correct_completion: public transport is much better for the environment.
full_sentence: Although many people prefer driving, public transport is much better for the environment.
acceptable_variants: public transport is still the better choice for the environment.
many people should consider buses and trains instead.

options.text: so they never use cars at all.
options.why_wrong: 'So' signals a result, not a contrast; after 'although' the clause must oppose the first part of the sentence.

options.text: public transport is much better for the environment.
cars are very expensive to buy.
options.why_wrong: This gives a fact about cars but supports the same side as the stem, so it does not express the contrast that 'although' requires.

options.text: they drive to work every day.
options.why_wrong: This repeats the preference already described in the stem instead of contrasting with it.

explanation: After 'although', the main clause must present a point that contrasts with the first part of the sentence. Learners often use 'so' or 'because' here because their first language may express cause and concession with similar patterns, but English keeps them separate.
